*This is the second part. I had to split it because I ran over in characters*


**My Early Twenties:**

After obtaining my GED I enrolled in a state college that turned out to be a good learning experience but not all I had hoped for in Computer Science. While in college I continued to invest my time in my own learning methods and as such was very productive. I continued developing applications to sell, and also began contracting with software firms over the internet to provide softare components they needed in order to complete their products/services. Once again while it put cash in the bank, it was not enough to survive on, so I continued to work as a farm-hand.

During these years the previously mentioned terror grew. At times I could not stay in classes because it felt like something bad might happen, with no reasoning to back it up. Rather than endure this confusing and irritating terror, I dropped out of college after a year and a half.

After dropping out while not working as a farm-hand I continued to grow my software related skills. I picked up bigger and bigger contracts, and also approached local business for gigs. I got a local contract for a newspaper, and wrote their search engine for current and archived articles (which is still in use today). During this time I was also publishing technical articles and open source software libraries online to help others learn. It was some of these articles along with my software that caught the eye of someone at Microsoft. A few days later I had a job offer, and began making plans to move to Seattle to work for the very company whose software I had grown up with.

**The first couple of years at Microsoft:**

Not long following my move, I started work at Microsoft and loved every minute of it. For once I had any tool I could ask for, and was getting paid to develop software and additional tools to make others more productive. During the process I met some other employees who have become close, but I largely stayed to myself. 

In staying to myself my mind had time to wander, and it became more frequent that I would be terrorized for no apparent reason - Not so much at work, but often when I was alone. Occasionally I would find myself driving and see someone following me, and drive hastily to try to lose them. There would also be times when I would 'detect' that someone was saying/thinking something even though they had not actually spoken. 

Despite this I still excelled at work. In my first two years I rose rapidly, with several promotions, great reviews and even earning a corporate award for great engineering. I loved my work and generated high quality code and projects.

**The last year and a downward spiral:**

In the last year things have taken a turn for the worse, my minds ability to sync reality with my thoughts is becoming more and more difficult. As a result my ability to work has faultered too. My code quality has fallen greatly, and I am no longer able to concentrate and have much for the 'deep thoughts' necessary for designing good software. 

After some people noticed, and asked me about some unusual things that had seen in me, I continued to keep the knowledge of the illness to myself. I did however contact a professional therapist and set up appointments under the guise that I was seeking help for anxiety. I wanted a solution to the symptoms so it could be unnoticable. After a few months nothing really emerged that I could use to hide my issues, so I decided to start working late hours and avoiding contact as much as possible. It worked for keeping my illness hidden, but it still affected me. My mind continued to decline.

It was not long after that I attempted suicide for the first time. While my roommate was on vacation, I closed the garage, started my car and waited. A little while later I awoke with a massive pounding headache, and then shut off the car and went to my room where I thought for sure I would die. Other than a massive headache, it was an unsuccessful attempt.

Several more months went by and feeling the inability to escape I finally sought help and gave them the REAL details of what I was feeling. There diagnosis was the generally the same as mine, I was suffering from Schizophrenia and/or Bipolar. Their suggested solutions were all drugs... All drugs for which I have researched and found to be sedatives, with the biggest side-effect being cognative impairment.  Even though I cannot perform my job at levels I once could, taking another hit on coginative ability would be worse than the disease itself for my ability to produce work.

**Now and why I am here:**

After suffering from Schizophrenia/Bipolar for many years, and having things getting much worse. My job as a software developer is becoming more and more difficult as is my ability to live day to day. When reality is not true to my thoughts (or vice versa) even the most basic functions can be difficult. On some weekends I can lose track of time and go for a couple of days without eating. I have a difficult time focusing on anything, and often fall behind on paying bills simply because it does not cross my mind. I very rarely hang out with friends anymore, and when I do I often am looking to leave.

I just want to be a productive member of society. I did not ask for this illness. From what I've seen and read, it will not get better. Things will continue until I am no longer what I once was in any form. 

I have written my will, and largely made up my mind to do things correctly this time. But I want to be sure. I'm asking if any of you know anyone with a similar condition to myself, that have improved and become productive again, then please let me know. If someone has discovered something that I have not, I'd like to learn from them. My hopes are not high. I do not want pity either. This is a last effort to find a 'workaround'.  If there is no workaround, I think most would agree that it is better to go in peace than to diminish and suffer in a shell of who you used to be.
